definition: Rolandic cortex is a part of the motor cortex involved in controlling movement. In the supplied source, altered activity and disrupted synchronization in this region are linked with motor impairment in children with epilepsy.

reasons: The definition’s first sentence claims that “Rolandic cortex is a part of the motor cortex involved in controlling movement,” but the supplied packet does not explicitly define Rolandic cortex as controlling movement (it mentions motor cortex and that oscillatory activity plays a role in cognition, perception and motor control, and it analyzes Rolandic cortex responses, but it does not make the requested definitional statement about movement control).

While the packet supports linking altered Rolandic cortex responses (excessive gamma-band activation) and ictal desynchronization with motor impairment in children with epilepsy, those points are not presented as a simple “altered activity and disrupted synchronization” definition for the term beyond what the study text shows.

The definition adds an unsupported anatomical claim that Rolandic cortex is a part of the motor cortex; the packet only shows it is a region from which motor-cortex responses were measured and does not define its location or equivalence.

The wording also goes beyond the packet by presenting Rolandic cortex as generally “involved in controlling movement,” whereas the source only reports an association between Rolandic activity and motor impairment in children with epilepsy.
